expected_effect: Steps +5% to +10% vs same-host control (roughly 2175-2280 steps) and public_val_bpb lower than the same-host control by 0.002 to 0.006 (target range 1.0000-1.0040 on trn21). Predeclared falsifier: if trigram tables carry more than ~0.005 BPB of the 0.020 table benefit at matched steps, the arm lands at or above control BPB despite the extra steps (FALSIFIED-QUALITY).
hypothesis: The hashed n-gram value-embedding tables are simultaneously the largest quality contributor and the largest per-step cost in the pinned configuration: removing all four tables buys +23% steps but costs +0.020 BPB (no-ngram-ve full), while halving the table byte budget by dim (dim64 smoke) buys ~+6% steps with no smoke-quality loss. The trigram tables (the half of the 4-table budget with the sparsest per-row training signal and the highest hash-collision rate at 1M rows over ~2k steps) are hypothesized to contribute the least quality per unit of table cost. Dropping only the trigram tables (bigram tables kept at both injection sites, same rows/dim) should recover a meaningful fraction of the no-ngram-ve throughput gain (+5% to +10% steps) while retaining most of the 0.020 BPB table benefit, yielding a net lower public_val_bpb at the fixed 1800 s budget.
single_causal_change: Pass --no-ngram-ve-trigram only. Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls: identical launch shape (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000, --max-train-seconds 1800, --seed 42), identical environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1), no precision flag (no --bf16-sdpa-input, --bf16-norm-output, --ngram-rms-fp32), no kernel or compile flag, no optimizer/schedule/batch/architecture/evaluation change, and no other ngram-ve option (--ngram-ve-dim stays 128, --ngram-ve-table-mult stays 128 -> rows 1048576, opt stays rmsprop, bf16 stays True, layers unchanged). The only behavioral delta is that trigram hashed tables are not instantiated or gathered; bigram tables remain at every default injection site. Pre-full check (from the smoke run's resolved ngram_ve oneliner and num_params_M): the control resolves 'True tables=4 rows=1048576 dim=128 ... trigram=True' with num_params_M 592.9; the candidate must resolve trigram=False with a reduced table count (expected tables=2) and reduced num_params_M (expected approximately 324.3, i.e. the same table budget as the dim64 arm allocated as 2 tables x 1048576 rows x 128 dim). If trigram still resolves True, or tables/num_params_M are unchanged (e.g. the flag only re-assigns all 4 tables to bigram hashes), classify FALSIFIED-INERT-COST and do not spend the full run; if tables resolves to some other reduced count, record the resolved value and continue only if num_params_M is below 592.9 by at least 25%. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 -> 2071 steps / 1.005734; trn22 -> 2076 steps / 1.005967). Outcome classes, mutually exclusive, evaluated in order: (1) FALSIFIED-INERT-COST as defined above; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if candidate steps < 90% of same-host control steps (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22; experiment-protocol.md section 5 rule; record as throughput regression only); (3) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if candidate steps > +10% of control (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): record throughput and BPB and require a matched-step sanity check against the control's logged trajectory before any quality claim (the controller's symmetric 10% rule as applied to the batch-ramp and no-ngram-ve arms); (4) FALSIFIED-NO-THROUGHPUT if steps are within +/-2% of control (trigram tables do not drive table cost); (5) SUCCESS if public_val_bpb < same-host control by at least 0.001 with steps >= control; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control (trigram quality contribution outweighs the recovered steps); (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. Secondary, non-verdict analysis: place this arm alongside the dim64 arm (4 x 1M x 64) and the prior mult64 evidence (4 x 512k x 128) as the third equal-budget allocation of ~268M table parameters, to attribute the table cost/quality trade to table count vs rows vs dim.
